key_takeaways: Funny wedding vows work when every laugh sets up a real promise: joke, turn, promise.
At a legal ceremony in Australia, your personal vows sit alongside the words the Marriage Act requires, never instead of them; your celebrant confirms the wording on the day.
Specific beats generic: humour drawn from your own shared life lands better than borrowed one-liners.
Keep the jokes kind: no humour about bodies, exes, money or anything that embarrasses your partner in front of family.
An Australian celebrant cannot perform a marriage overseas, so a ceremony they lead abroad is symbolic, and symbolic vows can be entirely your own.

faq.q: Can wedding vows be funny and still legal in Australia?
faq.a: Yes. The legal words in an Australian ceremony are a few set sentences; everything else, including your vows to each other, can carry as much humour as you like.

faq.q: How long should funny wedding vows be?
faq.a: Our guidance is about one minute each when spoken, roughly 120 to 180 words. Laughter adds time, so a 150-word vow with two good laughs can run longer than you expect. Time yourself reading aloud, then cut the weakest joke rather than the promise.

faq.q: Should we tell each other our vows before the wedding?
faq.a: It is your call. Some couples like the surprise; others want no surprises at all. A middle path: keep the words private, but each send your vows to your celebrant, who can check that the two are a similar length and tone without spoiling either.

faq.q: Can we use funny vows at a vow renewal?
faq.a: Yes, and with more freedom. Attorney-General's Department guidelines for celebrants say a renewal of vows is not a marriage: no Notice of Intended Marriage or marriage certificate is prepared, and witnesses are not required. Your celebrant confirms what the ceremony can say. For ideas, see our guide to writing vows for a renewal.

faq.q: What if one of us is funny and the other is not?
faq.a: Write to your own voice. A dry, sincere vow beside a funny one often makes both stronger, because the contrast is a portrait of you as a couple. Agree that neither vow will make the other the punchline, and let the funnier partner go first so the sincere vow lands last.
